content: Pyrethrin combined with piperonyl butoxide is a medication designed to eliminate parasites and their eggs. It is specifically used to treat infestations caused by scabies, as well as lice infestations affecting the head, body, and pubic area (commonly referred to as crabs). This medication is available in various forms, including liquid, gel, and shampoo. Typically, a single application is sufficient to address the infestation. However, in some cases, a second application may be necessary after one week if live parasites reappear. It is essential to follow the instructions provided on the packaging or prescription label meticulously. If there is any confusion, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the medication exactly as directed, avoiding overuse or underuse, and do not apply it more frequently than prescribed. If you have open cuts or scratches on your hands, wear rubber gloves while applying the medication. In the event of accidental contact with your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water for at least five minutes. For the liquid or gel form, follow these steps: 1. Apply enough medication to cover the affected hairy area and the surrounding regions. 2. Leave the medication on the skin for exactly 10 minutes. 3. Wash the treated area thoroughly with warm water and soap or regular shampoo. 4. Dry the area with a clean towel. 5. Wash your hands to remove any residual medication. 6. Change into clean clothes. For the shampoo form, follow these steps: 1. Shake the shampoo bottle well before use. 2. Apply the shampoo to dry hair and scalp or skin, ensuring complete coverage. 3. Add a small amount of water to create a lather. 4. Leave the shampoo on for exactly 10 minutes. 5. Rinse your hair thoroughly with water. 6. Dry your hair with a clean towel. 7. Use a fine-tooth comb to remove lice eggs (nits) and larvae. 8. Wash your hands to remove any residual medication. If treating head lice, clean combs and brushes by washing them with the liquid, gel, or shampoo, and rinse them thoroughly with water to remove any traces of the medication. Before using pyrethrin and piperonyl butoxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to pyrethrin, piperonyl butoxide, ragweed, petroleum products, or other medications. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. Pregnant individuals should wear gloves when applying this medication to another person to minimize skin absorption. This medication may cause side effects, including skin irritation, rash, redness, or swelling. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, contact your doctor. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Pyrethrin and piperonyl butoxide is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest the medication. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. After using the medication, machine-wash or dry-clean all clothing, bed linens, and towels used in the past two days. Use hot water and dry items in a hot dryer for at least 20 minutes. Thoroughly clean all bathtubs, showers, and toilets in your home with rubbing alcohol. Inform close contacts, including family members and sexual partners, that they may have been exposed to the parasites and advise them to seek medical attention if symptoms develop. If you are treating scabies, be aware that itching may persist for several weeks after treatment due to skin sensitivity to the parasite. This does not necessarily indicate treatment failure. Contact your doctor if you have concerns or questions. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have additional questions about its use.
